doc.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Goodman and Mingus as taskmasters
summary: Goodman's limits on harmonic freedom versus Mingus's demands and his lack of formal harmony.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Each one of these people, Goodman to Mingus, and I guess Sarah, had a reputation as being a taskmaster.
Was it a positive experience for most of it for you?

I think so. You know to answer that question I have to go back and remember my relationship with Benny. Benny was a great clarinetist. He could play any music, classical or jazz. But he had some restrictions on himself. He wouldn’t allow his jazz to be as free as it could have been. He was limited to the chord changes that had been played. He was not open to fresh chord changes. If you tried to do anything a little different, he’d say oh no, no, no, no. And he used to ask me to come up to the house just to play and play and play, so that he could try to open that door. But whenever we’d get to a song like “Again,” a simple song, and I’d throw in a few little — he said, “What’s that chord you just played, what’s that?” He’d ask me. And I’d say, “Well it’s just an F seventh going to a B flat minor.” He’d say, “Well don’t play that, isn’t that supposed to be C minor?” He couldn’t adjust to things like that. And Mingus on the other hand was a taskmaster in terms of getting guys to play a certain way for him. You know now he didn’t have that kind of schooling where he could tell what was supposed to be played. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

That’s why he kept practicing the piano, he was still trying to get his harmony chops. He used to call me late at night and ask me how to play a certain bridge or whatever. But the saxophone players that he had, he used to give them a hard time. He used to tell them, “No you’ve got to play the New Orleans type jazz,” you’ve got to do this, you’ve got to do that.
